facts.text: Two autonomous-haulage collisions in Western Australia in 2019 point to communications and traction failures rather than perception failures.
facts.quote: Two Western Australian collisions point to communications and traction failures rather than perception.

facts.text: At Fortescue's Christmas Creek mine in Western Australia on 11 February 2019, an autonomous truck reversed into a stationary truck.
facts.quote: At Fortescue's Christmas Creek mine on 11 February 2019 an autonomous truck reversed into a stationary one

facts.text: Press reports said the autonomous-truck collision at Fortescue's Christmas Creek mine on 11 February 2019 may have occurred after a dropout in Wi-Fi coverage.
facts.quote: press reports said the crash "may have occurred after a dropout in Wi-Fi coverage"

facts.text: Fortescue's chief executive stated that the autonomous-truck collision at Christmas Creek mine on 11 February 2019 was not the result of any failure of the autonomous system.
facts.quote: Fortescue's chief executive said "This was not the result of any failure of the autonomous system."

facts.text: For the 2019 collision at BHP's Jimblebar mine in Western Australia, the state regulator's director of mines safety said an unloaded autonomous truck lost traction and slid into the path of a loaded autonomous truck in bad weather.
facts.quote: the state regulator's director of mines safety said "an unloaded autonomous truck had lost traction and slid into the path of a loaded autonomous truck" in bad weather

facts.text: In the 2019 autonomous-truck collision at BHP's Jimblebar mine, the unloaded truck and loaded truck were travelling at about 14 km/h and 27 km/h respectively.
facts.quote: at about 14 km/h and 27 km/h respectively

facts.text: BHP confirmed that speed-restriction procedures had not been applied in connection with the 2019 bad-weather autonomous-truck collision at Jimblebar mine.
facts.quote: BHP confirmed it had not applied speed-restriction procedures.

facts.text: WA DMIRS followed up on interim controls for both the 11 February 2019 autonomous-truck collision at Fortescue's Christmas Creek mine and the 2019 autonomous-truck collision at BHP's Jimblebar mine.
facts.quote: The regulator (WA DMIRS) followed up on interim controls in both cases [38].
